guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / major bleeding and shock
title: Knife attack and wrist slash at a music festival
setting: Music festival. 20M teenager rushed into the first aid tent by friends. Slender bladed wound to the wrist, active spurting blood, bone visible.
verdictExplanation: Spurting arterial wrist bleed, partial hand amputation, and severe hypovolemic shock (PR 110 bpm, BP 75/51, deteriorating ACVPU). Sick: immediate arterial occlusion and 999.

shared.danger: Attacker's whereabouts are unknown (ensure security/police are called)
shared.response: Alert but rapidly becoming drowsy and weak
shared.catHaem: Spurting, rapid arterial bleeding from wrist wound
shared.circulation: Very weak and rapid pulse, skin is extremely cold, clammy, and pale

history.history: Assaulted by an attacker with a knife 5 minutes ago in the park area. A bystander has been applying direct pressure but cannot control the bleeding.
history.injuries: Large deep laceration on the inside of the right wrist, partial amputation
history.additional: Friend reports the attacker fled the scene

followUp.question: Which set of findings best indicates that this patient is in severe, decompensated hypovolaemic shock?

options.text: Dropping ACVPU level, blood pressure of 75/51, and cold/clammy skin
Pulse rate of 110 bpm and a pain score of 10/10
A respiration rate of 28/min and oxygen saturations of 87%
The presence of spurting arterial blood and partial hand amputation

followUp.explanation: Severe (decompensated) hypovolaemic shock is marked by inadequate brain perfusion (dropping ACVPU) and profound hypotension (75/51 mmHg). While tachycardia, pain, and the wound itself indicate injury and early shock, the key red flags of decompensation are the altered mental status and low blood pressure.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Apply direct pressure immediately. If a tourniquet is available in the kit and bleeding is catastrophic, apply high and tight on the arm. Call 999 and lie him flat.
levelFlags.erNotes: Catastrophic arterial haemorrhage. Apply tourniquet high on the single bone (humerus) of the upper arm, tighten until bleeding stops, write the time. Treat for hypovolemic shock with high-flow oxygen, keeping him warm, and arrange immediate priority transfer.
